questions.q:
In Faraday-Henry's experiment, a coil is connected to a galvanometer. For the deflection of pointer in the galvanometer, which of the following statement/s is/are WRONG?
The pointer in the galvanometer deflects -
(a) When the bar magnet is moved towards the stationary coil along its axis
(b) When the bar magnet is moved away from the stationary coil along its axis
(c) When the coil is moved towards the stationary bar magnet along its axis
(d) When the coil and the magnet are moved without relative motion between them
questions.explanation: The galvanometer deflects whenever there is relative motion between coil and magnet, so (a), (b) and (c) are correct. With no relative motion there is no flux change and hence no deflection, so only statement (d) is wrong.

questions.q: In the figure shown, the conductor PQ of length $l$ is moved from $x=0$ to $x=b$ and then up to $x=2b$ with a constant velocity $\vec v$. A uniform magnetic field $\vec B$ is perpendicular to the plane of the paper and extends from $x=0$ to $x=b$ and it is zero from $x>b$. The magnitude of emf induced in the conductor is [Figure: a rectangular conducting rail with rod PQ sliding along it with velocity $\vec v$; magnetic field $\vec B$ (dots, out of the page) fills the region from $x=0$ to $x=b$ and is zero beyond $x=b$]
questions.explanation: While the rod is within the field region ($0\le x\le b$) it cuts field lines and an emf $Blv$ is induced; beyond $x=b$, where the field is zero, no emf is induced.

questions.q: When a bar magnet is pushed towards the coil, along its axis, as shown in the figure, the galvanometer pointer deflects towards X. When this magnet is pulled away from the coil, the galvanometer pointer
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law, reversing the relative motion of the magnet reverses the induced EMF and current, so the galvanometer deflects the other way, towards X$^1$.

questions.q: A square loop of side 2 m lies in the Y-Z plane in a region having a magnetic field $\vec B=(5\hat i+3\hat j-4\hat k)$T. The magnitude of magnetic flux through the square loop is
questions.explanation: The loop's normal is along $\hat i$ (x-direction) since it lies in the Y-Z plane. Flux $=B_x A=5\times(2^2)=20$ Wb.

questions.q: In the figure, a conducting ring of certain resistance is falling towards a current carrying straight long conductor. The ring and conductor are in the same plane. Then the [ring A falls vertically towards a horizontal wire B carrying current I to the right]
questions.explanation: As the ring falls closer to the wire, the flux linking it increases, so by Lenz's law the induced current flows clockwise to oppose the increasing flux.

questions.q: An induced current of 2 A flows through a coil. The resistance of the coil is $10\Omega$. What is the change in magnetic flux associated with the coil in 1 ms ?
questions.explanation: $e=iR=2\times10=20\,V=\dfrac{d\phi}{dt}\Rightarrow d\phi=20\times10^{-3}=2\times10^{-2}\,Wb$.

questions.q: A square loop of side length 'a' is moving away from an infinitely long current carrying conductor at a constant speed 'v' as shown. Let 'x' be the instantaneous distance between the long conductor and side AB. The mutual inductance (M) of the square loop - long conductor pair changes with time (t) according to which of the following graphs? [square loop of side a, with side AB at distance x from a long straight current-carrying wire, moving away with speed v]
options: M decreases with a convex curve, approaching the t-axis
M decreases linearly to zero with t
questions.explanation: $M=\dfrac{\mu_0a}{2\pi}\ln\!\left(\dfrac{x+a}{x}\right)$ with $x=x_0+vt$; this decreases in a convex, non-linear way and asymptotically approaches zero as t increases.

questions.q: The current in a coil changes from 2A to 5A in 0.3s. The magnitude of emf induced in the coil is 1.0 V. The value of self-inductance of the coil is

A metallic rod of length 1 m held along east-west direction is allowed to fall down freely. Given horizontal component of earth's magnetic field B$_H$ = 3 × 10$^{-5}$ T. The emf induced in the rod at an instant t = 2s after it is released is (Take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$)

A square loop of side 2 cm enters a magnetic field with a constant speed of 2 cm s$^{-1}$ as shown [square loop of side 2 cm moving right with speed 2 cm/s into a field region of width 10 cm, B=0.5 T into the page]. The front edge enters the field at t = 0s. Which of the following graph correctly depicts the induced emf in the loop? (Take clockwise direction positive)
options: Triangular rise to 2×10$^{-4}$ V from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, negative triangular dip from 5 to 6s
Negative triangular dip from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, positive triangular rise to 2×10$^{-4}$ V from 5 to 6s
Constant −2×10$^{-4}$ V step from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, constant +2×10$^{-4}$ V step from 5 to 6s
Constant +2×10$^{-4}$ V step from t=0 to 1s, zero from 1 to 5s, constant −2×10$^{-4}$ V step from 5 to 6s
questions.explanation: While entering (0 to 1s) and leaving (5 to 6s) the field, a constant emf of magnitude Blv = 0.5×0.02×0.02 = 2×10$^{-4}$ V is induced with opposite signs, and it is zero while the loop is fully inside the field (1 to 5s), matching option C.

questions.q: A long solenoid has 500 turns, when a current of 2 A is passed through it, the resulting magnetic flux linked with each turn of the solenoid is 4 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ Wb, then self induction of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: $L=\dfrac{N\phi}{I}=\dfrac{500\times4\times10^{-3}}{2}=1.0$ H.

questions.q: A magnetic field of flux density 1.0 Wb m$^{-2}$ acts normal to a 80 turn coil of 0.01 m$^2$ area. If this coil is removed from the field in 0.2 second, the emf induced in it is
questions.explanation: emf $=\dfrac{N B A}{t}=\dfrac{80\times1.0\times0.01}{0.2}=4$ V.

questions.q: The current flowing through an inductance coil of self inductance 6 mH at different time instants is as shown: current rises from 0 at t = 0 to about 4 A near t = 20 s, then decreases through about 2 A near t = 40 s, continuing to fall towards zero afterward. The emf induced between t = 20s and t = 40s is nearly
questions.explanation: Using $|\varepsilon|=L\left|\dfrac{\Delta I}{\Delta t}\right|=6\times10^{-3}\times\dfrac{2}{20}=6\times10^{-4}$ V; readings of the current values off the graph are imprecise, which is likely why the KEA gave grace marks for this question. Option (C) is closest in order of magnitude and is taken as the answer per the KEA key.

questions.q: The physical quantity which is measured in the unit of wb A$^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: The henry (Wb/A) is the SI unit of both self-inductance and mutual inductance.

questions.q: A rod of length 2 m slides with a speed of 5 ms$^{-1}$ on a rectangular conducting frame as shown in figure [rod PQ of length 2 m moves at 5 m/s on rails, inside a uniform field of 0.04 T into the page, rod resistance 3 $\Omega$]. There exists a uniform magnetic field of 0.04 T perpendicular to the plane of the figure. If the resistance of the rod is 3 $\Omega$, the current through the rod is
questions.explanation: EMF $=Blv=0.04\times2\times5=0.4$ V, so current $=0.4/3=0.133$ A $=133$ mA.

questions.q: The current in a coil of inductance 0.2 H changes from 5 A to 2 A in 0.5 sec. The magnitude of the average induced emf in the coil is
questions.explanation: $|\varepsilon|=L\dfrac{dI}{dt}=0.2\times\dfrac{3}{0.5}=1.2$ V.

questions.q: [Figure shows a region of magnetic field into the page (crosses) with a wire AB slid on fixed horizontal rails towards the left with constant velocity v, connected to a resistor at the right end] Consider the situation given in figure. The wire AB is slid on the fixed rails with a constant velocity. If the wire AB is replaced by a semicircular wire, the magnitude of the induced current will
options: increase or decrease depending on whether the semicircle bulges towards the resistance or away from it
questions.explanation: The induced EMF depends only on the rate of change of the enclosed area, which is set by the perpendicular separation of the rails (effective length), not the shape of the sliding wire, so the current stays the same.

questions.q: A jet plane having a wing-span of 25 m is travelling horizontally towards east with a speed of 3600 km/hour. If the Earth's magnetic field at the location is 4 × 10$^{-4}$ T and the angle of dip is 30°, then, the potential difference between the ends of the wing is
questions.explanation: The vertical component of B is B$_v$ = B sin30° = 2×10$^{-4}$ T. Speed v = 3600 km/h = 1000 m/s. emf = B$_v$·v·l = 2×10$^{-4}$×1000×25 = 5 V.

questions.q: The magnetic flux linked with a coil varies as $\phi$ = 3t² + 4t + 9. The magnitude of the emf induced at t = 2 seconds is
A bar magnet is allowed to fall vertically through a copper coil placed in a horizontal plane [magnet's S pole leading, falling towards the coil]. The magnet falls with a net acceleration
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law, the induced eddy current in the coil opposes the magnet's motion, producing a retarding force, so the net downward acceleration is less than g.

questions.q: The working of magnetic braking of trains is based on
questions.explanation: Magnetic braking uses eddy currents induced in a conductor moving through a magnetic field, which oppose the motion and provide a braking force.

questions.q: A jet plane of wing span 20 m is travelling towards west at a speed of 400 ms$^{-1}$. If the earth's total magnetic field is $4\times10^{-4}$ T and the dip angle is 30°, at that place, the voltage difference developed across the ends of the wing is
questions.explanation: The vertical component of earth's field, $B_v = B\sin30° = 2\times10^{-4}$ T, drives the motional EMF: $\varepsilon = B_vLv = 2\times10^{-4}\times20\times400 = 1.6$ V.

questions.q: In the A.C. circuit shown, keeping 'K' pressed, if an iron rod is inserted into the coil, the bulb in the circuit, [circuit with a bulb and a coil in series with an AC source and switch K, and an iron rod that can be inserted into the coil]
options: glows with same brightness (as before the rod is inserted)
questions.explanation: Inserting the iron core increases the coil's self-inductance, increasing its inductive reactance and hence the circuit impedance, so the current — and the bulb's brightness — decreases.

questions.q: A wheel with 10 spokes each of length 'L' m is rotated with a uniform angular velocity '$\omega$' in a plane normal to the magnetic field 'B'. The emf induced between the axle and the rim of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Each spoke is a rotating rod of length L generating the same emf $\dfrac{1}{2}B\omega L^2$; since all spokes are in parallel (identical emf sources between axle and rim), the net emf equals that of a single spoke, independent of the number of spokes N.

questions.q: Two coils have a mutual inductance 0.005 H. The current changes in the first coil according to the equation $i=i_m\sin\omega t$ where $i_m=10$ A and $\omega=100\pi$ rad s$^{-1}$. The maximum value of the emf induced in the second coil is
questions.explanation: $\varepsilon_{max}=Mi_m\omega=0.005\times10\times100\pi=5\pi$ V.

questions.q: An aircraft with a wingspan of 40 m flies with a speed of 1080 km/hr in the eastward direction at a constant altitude in the northern hemisphere, where the vertical component of the earth's magnetic field is $1.75\times10^{-5}$ T. Then the emf developed between the tips of the wings is
A solenoid of inductance 2H carries a current of 1 A. What is the magnetic energy stored in a solenoid?
questions.explanation: U = \dfrac{1}{2}LI^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\times2\times1^2 = 1 J.

questions.q: Two identical circular coils A and B are kept on a horizontal tube side by side without touching each other. If the current in the coil A increases with time, in response, the coil B
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law, the current induced in B opposes the increasing flux from A, which makes the facing sides of A and B act like similar magnetic poles, so B is repelled.

questions.q: A rectangular coil of 100 turns and size 0.1 m $\times$ 0.05 m is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.1 T. If the field drops to 0.05 T in 0.05 second, the magnitude of the e.m.f. induced in the coil is
questions.explanation: $\text{EMF}=NA\,\dfrac{dB}{dt}=100\times0.005\times\dfrac{0.05}{0.05}=0.5\ \text{V}=\sqrt{0.25}\ \text{V}$, which does not match any of the given square-root options; KEA granted grace marks for this question.

questions.q: Direction of current induced in a wire moving in a magnetic field is found using
questions.explanation: Fleming's right hand rule gives the direction of induced current for a conductor moving in a magnetic field (motional EMF).

questions.q: The energy stored in an inductor of self inductance $L$ henry carrying a current of $I$ ampere is ............
questions.explanation: The energy stored in an inductor is $U=\dfrac{1}{2}LI^2$.

questions.q: There is a uniform magnetic field directed perpendicular and into the plane of the paper. An irregular shaped conducting loop is slowly changing into a circular loop in the plane of the paper. Then .........................
options: AC is induced in the loop.
no current is induced in the loop.
current is induced in the loop in the anti-clockwise direction.
current is induced in the loop in the clockwise direction.
questions.explanation: As the irregular loop reshapes into a circle (which encloses the maximum area for a given perimeter), the flux into the page increases; by Lenz's law the induced current opposes this increase, flowing anticlockwise to produce an outward field.

questions.q: Near a circular loop of conducting wire an electron moves along a straight line [passing below the loop, moving from right to left, as shown in the figure]. The direction of the induced current if any in the loop is
questions.explanation: As the electron approaches and then recedes from the loop, the flux through the loop first increases then decreases (and reverses as it passes), so by Lenz's law the induced current direction is variable.
